correctness.rationale: The orbit bound applies with tie retention: in ±1 spins take the symmetric adjacency matrix plus a unit self-weight at the even-degree hub only. All local fields are nonzero and their signs give the stated update. The two-time energy −x(t+1)^T B x(t) is decreasing strictly whenever x(t+1)≠x(t−1), so on a periodic orbit the period divides two. With a zero hub the second rim update is AND on the site and its distance-two neighbors, forcing occupation to be constant on step-two cycles. Hub consistency leaves the zero state and, for even n, one exchanged checkerboard pair. Complementation gives the fixed-one-hub cases. On a flipping orbit choose its unique zero-hub phase: the second rim update gives x_i(x_(i−2)∨x_(i+2)). Consequently no one may be isolated and the hub updates require 2s>n and 2e<n. For a nonconstant labelled cyclic word, marking a one-run gives L starting positions and compositions of s into b lengths at least two and L−s into b positive lengths, divided by b markings; e=s−b. Constant words contribute the two stated monomials, including the directed-pair convention for L=2. The step-two factors multiply at even n. The two length-two components at n=4 force s=e; a single run of (n+1)/2 for odd n, or runs 2 and n/2−1 on the two components for even n≥6, meet both strict inequalities. The independent exhaustive Boolean iteration reproduced the complete displayed counts through n=14.
residual_risks: The independent census is finite; the energy and run arguments give the all-size result.
